title: Transient role shadowing after RBAC v2 migration causing intermittent denies or over-grants and missing audit events
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary: After the RBAC v2 migration and a SAML group-sync rollout, several customers reported intermittent permission denied errors followed by short-lived over-permissioned sessions. In parallel we observed missing audit events for the window where the mismatch occurs. This ticket tracks investigation, root cause, and a safe rollout plan to eliminate the transient role-shadowing race and ensure audit completeness.

Impact: Multiple customers (enterprise and Dedicated) reported user-facing failures: admin consoles returning 403s for users who should have access, and in one case a user temporarily gained elevated access (short-lived, <30s) during a sync window. Audit logs do not contain a reliable trail for the exact granted/denied transitions for those windows, complicating escalations and compliance reviews.

How to reproduce (staging):
1) Configure RBAC v2 migration mode and enable incremental SAML group sync.
2) Trigger a concurrent role binding change via the admin API while a SAML group-sync for the same account is in-flight (simulate with two requests separated by ~10-40ms).
3) Observe that the authorization cache update path applies in the wrong order in ~2-3% of attempts, leading to either a transient deny or an overgrant.
4) Observe audit emitter sometimes drops the intermediate event when buffer flush is preempted by a parallel GC/flush, leaving only the final state in logs.

Root cause hypothesis: Two issues together: (1) optimistic in-memory role cache invalidation in the edge auth service that applies operations out-of-order under concurrency (we used last-write-win without strict monotonic versioning), and (2) the audit emitter batches events and uses a non-durable buffer which can be preempted by a concurrent flush/rotation, causing loss of short-lived intermediate audit events. The race window is small but reproducible under load and subject to timing on cloud VMs.

Proposed fixes:
- Hotfix (short term): Force synchronous audit flush for role-change operations when migration flag is enabled and when operation touches admin-level bindings. Roll this as a limited canary to affected customers in Dedicated. (Pros: quick; Cons: latency spike on role changes).
- Medium: Add monotonic version tokens to role-binding operations and require compare-and-apply semantics on the cache update path. This ensures deterministic ordering even with concurrent operations.
- Long term: Replace non-durable audit buffer with a small durable queue (append-only) for RBAC events until ack from persistence layer. Backpressure if queue grows.

Acceptance criteria:
- No reproducible transient deny/overgrant in stress tests (100k trial runs, <0.001% failure).
- All role-change windows produce complete audit events for both intermediate and final states in the audit store for at least 30 days retention in staging.
- Canary rollout to 3 internal tenants then 2 paying customers without any new escalations.

Testing plan:
- Add deterministic concurrency test in platform/auth with mocked SAML sync and admin API to assert ordering semantics.
- Load test the synchronous audit flush path to quantify latency penalty.
- Run chaos tests with small network jitter to increase race surface.

Rollout plan:
1) Deploy hotfix synchronous-audit flush to canary environment (canary group: internal + staging).
2) Monitor canary for 48 hours; key metrics: auth_403_rate_change, audit_event_loss_rate, role_update_latency.
3) If stable, release to Dedicated customers behind opt-in flag.
4) Deploy monotonic version tokens in next release with gradual rollout and compatibility shim.

Monitoring & dashboards:
- Add Grafana panels: auth.cache.apply_order_skew, audit.emitter.dropped_events, role.change.latency_p50/p99.
- Alert: audit.emitter.dropped_events > 1/min for >5m for any production cluster -> P0 oncall.

Customer comms:
- Draft escalations to affected customers explaining root cause and mitigation plan; offer customer-level rollback for migration if requested.

Links & artifacts:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/RBAC+V2+Migration+Postmortem
- GitHub PR (hotfix): https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/12345
- Staging dashboard (read-only): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/rbac/role-sync-summaries

Notes and trade-offs: synchronous audit flush is likely to add 50-150ms to admin binding changes but those operations are infrequent. Monotonic tokens require coordinated changes across services that read/write role bindings (auth service, syncer, migrations). We must be careful with rollback semantics to avoid further divergence in active sessions.
